summary:
Approve with non-blocking suggestions. No correctness regression found. Reported two comments: clarify the cached full-list naming and assert caller-visible results in the mixed-history test.

Validation: all 65 LanguageModel tests passed. A plain-node probe passed for both APIs, covering mixed approval history, distinct approval/tool-call IDs, result emission, replay without re-execution, and provider prompt cleanup. Results were appended to both finding threads. The probe was removed; the working tree is clean.

Full-suite, check, and lint commands were not run, per the review constraints.

params.title: Name the cached full list allApproved rather than allResolved
params.body: Optional naming cleanup: the `approved` array returned by the collector includes pending approvals too, so `allResolved` is not yet a resolved-only list at this point. Using `allApproved` in both request paths would make its relationship to `allDenied` and `pendingApproved` explicit and avoid suggesting that it is safe to execute the entire list. The current behavior is correct; this is just clarity for the newly cached state.

params.title: Also assert the results returned from mixed approval history
params.body: Optional regression coverage: this new mixed-history test discards the generated response and drains the stream, so it verifies handler execution and the provider prompt but not which pre-resolved results reach the caller. Capture the response/stream parts and assert that only `pending-approved` and `pending-denied` are emitted, once each, with the expected failure flags. The existing stream emission test covers only a single pending approved call, not the resolved/pending and approved/denied partition exercised here.

Validation: all 65 tests in `pnpm test --run packages/effect/test/ai/LanguageModel.test.ts` passed. The plain-node mixed-history probe passed for both APIs and confirmed that the full approved list contains entries whose tool results are only added during pre-resolution; no functional issue was observed.

Probe result: `node scratchpad/pr-9143-approvals.ts` passed for both generateText and streamText with distinct approval IDs and tool-call IDs. Each emitted exactly the newly approved and newly denied result (failure flags false/true); replay emitted no tool results and did not re-execute the handler. Both provider requests retained four tool results and no resolved approval artifacts. This is a request to retain that coverage in the checked-in test, not a demonstrated bug.
